part.text: The file covers all of 2013–2025, and the pedestrian-fatality field has no missing values. I’m using annual sums of that field, which directly count pedestrians killed rather than crashes involving a death.

input.command:
python -c 'import os, duckdb, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
os.makedirs("out", exist_ok=True)
df=duckdb.query("SELECT year(crash_date) AS year, CAST(sum(number_of_pedestrians_killed) AS BIGINT) AS pedestrian_deaths FROM read_parquet('\''data/crashes.parquet'\'') WHERE crash_date >= DATE '\''2013-01-01'\'' AND crash_date < DATE '\''2026-01-01'\'' GROUP BY year ORDER BY year").df()
df.to_csv("out/values_1.csv", index=False)
fig, ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(10,5.5))
ax.bar(df["year"].astype(str), df["pedestrian_deaths"], color="#3b82a0")
ax.set_title("Pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes by year")
ax.set_xlabel("Crash year")
ax.set_ylabel("Pedestrians killed")
ax.set_ylim(0, max(df["pedestrian_deaths"])*1.18)
ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=.25)
for i,v in enumerate(df["pedestrian_deaths"]): ax.text(i,v+2,str(v),ha="center",va="bottom",fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("out/option_1.png", dpi=180)
plt.close(fig)
print(df.to_string(index=False))'
